Setup.Name: Kingdom Setup
Setup.Label: Open Setup
Setup.Hint: Seats, advisors, table options and the story import.

TapTreasury.Name: Tap Treasury
TapTreasury.Hint: The only way to turn kingdom funds into gold. It creates a debt, adds Corruption and Unrest, and is logged by name.

PinResolved.Name: Resolved event pins
PinResolved.Hint: What happens to a map pin once its event is over.

DeskMatters.Name: Weekly desk matters
DeskMatters.Hint: Each week, a small matter lands on whichever desk has been quietest. The month's major events are drawn as usual.

Audiences.Name: Monthly audiences
Audiences.Hint: Each month a petitioner comes before one seat holder, who answers in person.

Council.Name: Council
Council.Hint: Projects can be proposed to the council for votes, and a reminder posts at the start of each month.

PinsShown.Name: Show new map pins to players
PinsShown.Hint: Off: a card's pin on the Stolen Lands map is GM-only until you show it with the eye button. On: pins of new cards are shown to players straight away (secret events stay hidden), and the eye hides them. Lots of pins can make the map's own notes harder to click.

Setup.Title: Kingdom Setup
Setup.AdventureImported: Adventure has been imported into this world
Setup.SeatsHint: Give each seat a holder: a player character, an NPC actor, or a companion advisor. Seats held by advisors need a player to supervise them, so every desk has someone at the table looking after it.
Setup.ShowingCompanions: Holders are limited to the party and Kingmaker companions.
Setup.ShowingAll: Showing every actor in the world.
Setup.FoundingHint: The party picks two realm stats the kingdom was built around. Each starts at rank 1. This is set once; you can undo it and pick again.
Setup.FoundingResetConfirm: Take back the founding focus? Both stats lose the rank and points it gave them.
Setup.FoundingIncomplete: Pick two different stats for the founding focus, or leave both empty.
Setup.ToolsNotice: Kingdom Building, Camping & Weather is active. Its camping and weather work fine alongside this module; just don't use its kingdom sheet, since Ultimate Kingdom Manager runs the kingdom.
Setup.AdvisorsHint: Companions and NPCs who can advise a seat. Tick Known once the party has met them; only known advisors are offered in the seat lists above. Add any other NPC at the bottom: start typing and the NPCs in this world are suggested (Jaethal, Nok-Nok, Jhod Kavken and Bokken, for example).
Setup.AdvisorNeedsName: Give the NPC a name and a seat.
Setup.CapitalHint: Found the capital here first: pick a settlement already on the map or name a new one. It comes with a free Founders' Hall (a home that also cuts the capital's food need by 1). Until there's a capital, no cards or projects appear.
Setup.CapitalDone: {name} is the capital. Change its name above; its tracks are managed on the Settlements tab. Renaming it here doesn't change the Kingmaker map: if the capital is drawn there, rename its label with the hex tool too.
Setup.KingdomNew: Saving Setup founds the kingdom: its name, its seats and its level (always the party's).
Setup.KingdomHint: The kingdom's numbers (Unrest, Ruin, Fame, level) are kept by the Kingdom Manager, not the PF2e kingdom sheet.
Setup.RulerHint: One player character wears the crown. The ruler isn't a seat: they also hold whatever seat they sit in, and they get the royal powers (Realm tab, The crown).

Import.Title: Import Story Content
Import.Intro: Copy regions, locations, kingdom events, quests, characters and structures from the Kingmaker adventure into GM-only journals in this world. This only needs doing once; the originals are not changed.
Import.Reimport: Content was imported before. Pages you have edited since then will be left as they are.
Import.NotReady: The Kingmaker module must be active and its adventure imported into this world.
Import.Counts: {created} pages created, {updated} updated, {skipped} kept because you edited them.
Import.Failed: The story import failed. See the console for details.

Manager.Title: Ultimate Kingdom Manager
Manager.NoKingdom: No kingdom has been founded yet. The GM founds it in Setup.
Manager.IncomeBreakdown: Base {base} · Work sites {worksites} · Economy rank {ranks} · Trade {trade} · Settlements {tracks} · Upkeep −{upkeep} · Food −{food} (need {need}, farms cover {farms})
Manager.DrawnNone: No events could be drawn right now.
Manager.RoutineHint: Everyday life in the realm. Grows faster when the stat is well behind what the kingdom's level allows.
Manager.AtCap: at the cap for this level
Manager.MatterNone: No desk matter fits right now.
Manager.StoryEventsHint: These come from the adventure's story, not the monthly draw. Put one on its desk when the story reaches it.
Manager.GmAway: No GM is online. You can read the desks, but nothing can be done until the GM is back.
Manager.AnyPlayerHint: Nobody at the table plays this seat, so any player can handle its cards and choices. Pick a supervising player in Setup to give it to one person.

Card.EscalateHint: Can be taken on by the party as an adventure
Card.NoPersonalSkill: None of your characters has a skill that fits this event.
Card.PersonalHint: A character takes this on in person, rolling their own skill against the same DC an advisor would face. A critical success earns Fame, and their player can reroll with a hero point. Anyone in the party can do it. Someone who doesn't hold this desk is lent to it: their own desk and this one take no other work until it's done, and their player makes the roll.
Card.EscalateConfirm: Take this to the table? The deadline pauses until the GM records how the party fared.
Card.DismissConfirm: Remove this card without applying any outcome?
Card.Working: {name} is on it — done in {days} days
Card.AdvisorBusy: The advisor is busy with another matter.
Card.Rolled: {name}'s roll: {result}. Reroll from the chat card, or accept it. It applies on its own after a day.
Card.HelpingChat: {name} is lent to the {seat}'s desk for {days} days. Until it's done, these desks take no other work: {desks}. {name}'s player makes the roll.
Card.DeskBusy: Desk tied up: someone is lent to {card}.
Card.ContinuousUntil: Ongoing: it comes back every month until {ends}.

Log.food-shortfall: The treasury could not cover food upkeep. Unrest rises.
Log.starting-point: The realm was set for a level {name} kingdom.
Log.kingdom-imported: Kingdom read from the PF2e kingdom sheet: {name}
Log.gm-adjust: The GM set the kingdom's numbers by hand

Resolve.Continues: This matter isn't over. It returns next month.
Resolve.RollFailed: Couldn't roll {name}. Check that the kingdom and skill are set up.
Resolve.Ignored: Nobody heard them out, and they went home angry.
Resolve.Windfall: A windfall: +{bp} BP to the treasury.
Resolve.AnarchyWorse: The realm is in anarchy: the result is one step worse.
Resolve.ContinuesUntil: This matter isn't over: it comes back next month until {ends}.

Request.Assigned: On it. Expect a result in {days} days.
Request.NoGM: No GM is online. Desk actions wait until the GM is back.

Reason.NotOpen: That card is no longer open.
Reason.NotYourCharacter: That character isn't in the party.
Reason.NoSkill: That character doesn't have that skill.
Reason.NotAssigned: Nobody is working on that card.
Reason.Timeout: The GM didn't answer. Try again.
Reason.NotReady: That stat isn't ready to rank up.
Reason.AlreadyUnderway: A rank-up for that stat is already underway.
Reason.TooPoor: The treasury needs {cost} BP for that.
Reason.NoTarget: That place isn't available for this project.
Reason.NoStructure: That building can't go up there now.
Reason.TapDisabled: Tapping the treasury is turned off.
Reason.InDebt: Economy can't rank up while the realm is in debt.
Reason.NotEnoughGold: That character doesn't have that much gold.
Reason.AdvisorOnly: Only the advisor can do this one.
Reason.NotRuler: Only the ruler's player (or the GM) can do that.
Reason.DeskBusy: The {desk} desk is tied up with {card}.
Reason.HasCapital: The realm already has a capital.
Reason.NameTaken: A settlement already has that name.
Reason.NotRolled: There's no result waiting on that card.
Reason.AlreadyRerolled: That check has already been rerolled.
Reason.NoFame: The realm has no Fame to spend.
Reason.AlreadyRolled: That flat check has already been rolled.
Reason.NoRuler: There's no ruler yet. Name one in Setup.
Reason.NoRoyalUse: That royal power has already been used this month.
Reason.AlreadyDecreed: This result has already been decreed.
Reason.NoFavour: That favour has already been used.
Reason.TrackWorking: That track is already being built there.
Reason.TrackPinnacleTaken: Another settlement already has that pinnacle.
Reason.TrackCapitalOnly: That can only be built in the capital.

Effect.IncomeHalved: Next month's income halved (at least {bp} BP lost)
Effect.BpDice: {amount} resource dice over the next month
Effect.ConsumptionSkip: No food upkeep for a month
Effect.Reroll: A reroll, kept for a month
Effect.ManualDetail: Apply by hand: see the event text for {detail}.
Effect.Repeat: It will come up again next month
Effect.RequireClaim: Claim a new hex within {days} days, or Unrest rises
Effect.ClaimMet: {card}: the new claim satisfied the demand.

Gm.retry: {card}: the party can try again as a project, at a higher DC.
Gm.leaderOut: {card}: if the target was a leader, they're out of action ({days} days, or for good on a critical failure). Clear the seat in Setup until they return.
Gm.settlementItemBonus: {card}: double the item bonuses of structures in {where} for {days} days.
Gm.breakRelations: {card}: relations with that group are broken. Reestablishing them is harder.
Gm.giftReturn: {card}: work out the return on the gifts the realm sent, as the event text describes.
Gm.blockArmies: {card}: armies can't be raised or moved here while the feud lasts.
Gm.check: {card}: roll a {skill} check as the event text describes and apply what it says.
Gm.requireProject: {card}: the realm must calm Unrest within {days} days or it rises.
Gm.claimHex: {card}: mark the hex as claimed with the Kingmaker hex tools.
Gm.offer: {card}: the settlers offer land for {cost} resource dice of BP. If the table accepts, take it from the treasury and mark the claim.
Gm.degreeBonus: {card}: craft and masterpiece checks are one degree better for {days} days.
Gm.freeProject: {card}: the realm may claim or improve {count} hex for free within {days} days.
Gm.freeStructure: {card}: build a {structures} in {where} for free within {days} days.
Gm.replaceLeader: {card}: replace the disgraced leader, or the scandal comes back.
Gm.taint: {card}: the leader is tainted for a while; more scandals may follow.
Gm.noModGrowth: {card}: the next outbreak doesn't get harder.

Effect.RerollMany: {uses} rerolls on these checks, kept for {days} days
Effect.FlatPending: Flat check DC {dc}: roll it from the chat card
Effect.FlatWhy: Fate decides the rest: roll a flat check, DC {dc}.
Effect.BpOverMonth: {amount} BP, paid over the next month
Effect.BpDiceRoll: {amount} × {per} BP, paid over the next month

Rank.RaisedDetail: Advisors now roll {skills} as {prof}: +{bonus}, plus the kingdom's level.
Rank.BeginConfirm: Spend {cost} BP and two weeks of the seat's advisor's time? The advisor can't take cards until it's done ({days} days).
Rank.Started: The rank-up is underway. It takes {days} days.
Rank.Choosing: Rank-up ready: a choice is waiting
Rank.ReadyText: The seat's holder has a choice to make on the Realm tab.
Rank.PreviewHint: This is what the seat will choose from when {stat} reaches rank {rank}. Nothing is spent or chosen here.

Project.Treasury: Treasury: {bp} BP. The cost is paid when the project starts.
Project.CampHint: On a hex with the matching resource the site pays double.

NoTargets.frontier: There are no unclaimed hexes next to the realm. If the kingdom has no hexes yet, the GM marks the first claim with the Kingmaker hex tools.
NoTargets.claimed-no-road: Every claimed hex already has a road.
NoTargets.claimed-no-farm: No claimed hex is free for farmland.
NoTargets.claimed-no-camp: No claimed hex is free for a work site.
NoTargets.settlement: The realm has no settlements yet.
NoTargets.claimed-not-fortified: Every claimed hex is already fortified.
NoTargets.claimed-no-settlement: Every claimed hex already has a settlement.

Project.NoStructures: No structures are known yet. Import the story content first.
Project.Started: The project is on the desk. {cost} BP paid. Delegate it or handle it personally.

Task.fortifyPick: Fortify {where}: open that hex on the map and tick Fortified in its Kingdom section.

Project.WhereHint: Tell the GM which hex. A note here goes into the GM's task.
Project.WherePlaceholder: e.g. east of Monkeyton, by the river

Tap.Title: Tap the treasury
Tap.Hint: The only way to turn kingdom money into gold for the party. It leaves a debt.
Tap.Explain: Draw up to {gold} gp for one character. It costs {cost} BP, and on any draw the realm gains 1 Unrest and 1 Corruption, a debt of the gold taken, and a public record of who took it. Until the debt is repaid, weekly income drops by a quarter, Economy can't rank up, and every further draw is two degrees worse with a chance of scandal.
Tap.DebtWarning: The realm already owes {debt} gp. This draw is two degrees worse and may cause a scandal.
Tap.NeedsApproval: The GM has to approve this.
Tap.ApprovalAsk: {user} wants to tap the treasury: {gold} gp for {actor}, costing {cost} BP. Allow it?
Tap.Consequences: The treasury loses {cost} BP. Unrest +1, Corruption +1, and the realm now owes the gold back.
Tap.WorseInDebt: With the realm already in debt, it went two degrees worse.
Tap.Scandal: Word got out. A Public Scandal has landed on the Ruler's desk.
Tap.GiveByHand: Add the gold to the character sheet by hand.
Tap.DebtHint: Repay it with gold from the party. Until then: income −25%, Economy can't rank up, further draws are worse.
Tap.RepayExplain: The realm owes {debt} gp. Gold comes off the character's sheet.
Tap.Repaid: {actor} pays {gold} gp back into the treasury. {left} gp still owed.
Tap.Cleared: {actor} pays {gold} gp and clears the realm's debt.

Council.Intro: Projects proposed to the council wait here. Everyone can vote; the Ruler decides what gets funded.
Council.Empty: Nothing before the council. Propose a project from a desk's Start project button.
Council.Off: The council is turned off in the module settings.
Council.MeetsWaiting: {count} proposals are waiting, and the treasury holds {bp} BP.
Council.MeetsEmpty: Nothing is waiting on the council this month. The treasury holds {bp} BP.
Council.DecisionFunded: {ruler} funds {name} ({cost} BP). The council voted {yes} for, {no} against. Work starts on its desk.
Council.DecisionRejectedTitle: The crown turns down a proposal
Council.DecisionRejected: {ruler} turns down {name}. The council voted {yes} for, {no} against.
Council.ProposeOrStart: Start it now from the treasury, or put it to the council?

Ambition.Heading: Seat ambitions

Goal.successes: Handle {n} matters on this desk successfully
Goal.structures: Build {n} settlement track stages (+1 and up) across the realm
Goal.projects: Finish {n} roads, farms or settlement stages

Ambition.What: Each desk has a long-term goal, such as handling three matters on that desk successfully. Reach it for a reward; then a harder goal takes its place.

Handbook.Missing: The handbook hasn't been set up yet. The GM needs to log in once with this version of the module.
Handbook.PlayersOnly: none (a party member or a hired advisor)

Pins.FortifiedHint: Threats don't appear on fortified hexes.

Hired.Name: Hired advisor
Hired.Hint: A hired advisor fills an empty seat: the desk can delegate, and the stat grows each week. They roll at −2, have no special ability, and cost 1 BP a week.

Attitude.Heading: Companion attitudes
Attitude.Hint: Set as their Influence changes in play. Below friendly, a companion won't use their special ability. Below indifferent, they stop advising altogether.

Bonus.Wasted: Adds nothing right now: these checks already get a +{existing} status bonus, and status bonuses don't stack.
Bonus.Partial: Only adds +{gain} right now: these checks already get a +{existing} status bonus, and status bonuses don't stack.
Bonus.Converted: The status bonus wouldn't have added anything here, so it became two rerolls on the same checks instead.
Bonus.WillConvert: Its status bonus would add nothing here (these checks already have one, and status bonuses don't stack), so it becomes two rerolls on the same checks instead.
Bonus.AdvisorTip: An advisor rolls like a character of the kingdom's level who is {prof} in these skills: level + proficiency + a good attribute. Settlement tracks add item bonuses, a companion a status bonus.

Settlement.NowOvercrowded: {name} is now overcrowded: it needs more homes (houses, tenements and other residential buildings), or it adds 1 Unrest a month.
Settlement.CapitalTask: Found the capital {name}: claim {where} if it isn't already, and mark a village named {name} there.
Settlement.CapitalChat: The realm has its heart. Settlers raise the first homes and the banners go up. From here the kingdom grows.
Settlement.FirstStep: Every kingdom starts with a capital. Pick a settlement already on the map or name a new one. Until the capital is founded the desks stay quiet and no projects can start. The capital starts with Huts, a Campfire and a Shrine.
Settlement.FirstStepWait: The GM founds the capital as part of setting up the kingdom.
Settlement.Name: Name
Settlement.Waterside: On a river, lake or swamp
Settlement.WatersideHint: Waterside settlements can use mills and piers to their full effect.
Settlement.UseMap: Make this settlement on the map the capital
Settlement.Overcrowded: Overcrowded: +1 Unrest a month until it has more homes.
Settlement.GrowNeeds: Becomes a {type} at kingdom level {level}, once {lots} lots are built and it has enough homes.
Settlement.RemoveConfirm: Remove {name} from {settlement}? Use this for rubble or a building the story destroyed.
Settlement.DeleteConfirm: Remove {name} from the realm? Its buildings go with it. The map isn't changed.
Settlement.NoRoom: No building fits in {name} right now. It needs to grow first, or the kingdom needs a higher level.
Settlement.PlaceHint: For buildings that were already standing before the module was installed. No cost, no roll, no Unrest or Fame.
Settlement.Unplaced: Not on the grid (no room left in a block that fits)

Start.Title: Joining mid-campaign
Start.Hint: Starting the module partway through the adventure? Set the realm where it would be by now.
Start.Intro: The party is level {level}. Set the realm where a well-run kingdom of that level would be. Rank-up choices from earlier ranks are skipped. You can come back here any time; nothing is ever lowered except the ranks you change.
Start.StatsHint: Suggested: the two founding stats at the cap ({cap}), filled seats one below, empty seats two below. Change any of them.
Start.TreasuryHint: Suggested: about a month of base income, or what's there now if it's more.
Start.Applied: The realm has been set for a level {level} kingdom.
Start.Nudge: The party is level {level} but every realm stat is still at rank 0. If you're starting the module partway through the adventure, set the realm's starting point here.

Fortune.Heading: Rerolls
Fortune.None: The realm has no rerolls right now. Some rewards give them.
Fortune.UseHint: Spend one of the realm's rerolls: roll this check again and keep the new result.
Fortune.What: Rerolls come from some rewards. When a card has rolled and the result is waiting, its seat can spend one to roll again; the new result stands, one reroll per check.
Fortune.UseFameHint: Spend a point of Fame to roll this check again. The new result stands.

Standing.FameAsk: The party can spend all its Fame ({fame}) to stop this. Spend it?
Standing.FameRuin: {ruin} is about to reach its limit and add a Ruin penalty.
Standing.FameAnarchy: Unrest is about to reach 20, and the realm would fall into anarchy.
Standing.FameSpent: The party spent all its Fame to hold off disaster.
Standing.Anarchy: Unrest has reached 20. The realm falls into anarchy: every kingdom check is one step worse until Unrest drops below 20.
Standing.Order: Unrest is below 20 again. The anarchy is over.
Standing.Trouble: With Unrest at 10 or more, things fall apart: {ruin}.
Standing.HexLost: Flat check {roll} against 11: a hex slips out of the realm's control. The GM marks it unclaimed.
Standing.HexHeld: Flat check {roll} against 11: the borders hold this month.
Standing.LoseHexTask: Unrest cost the realm a hex: unclaim one claimed hex of the party's choice on the map.
Standing.FlatWhy: Each month Unrest stays at 10 or more, the realm risks losing a hex: roll a flat check, DC 11. On a failure the GM unclaims a hex.

Royal.Heading: The crown
Royal.NoRuler: No ruler yet. The GM names one player character king or queen in Setup.
Royal.DecreeHint: Once a month: roll a waiting result again and keep the better of the two. Use it from the card.
Royal.DecreeBetter: {ruler} decrees it so: {card} is rolled again, and the better result stands.
Royal.DecreeKept: {ruler} decrees it so: {card} is rolled again, but the first result was better and stands.
Royal.CourtHint: Once a month: hold court in the capital and hear the people out. Unrest −1.
Royal.CourtChat: {ruler} holds court and hears the people out. Unrest −1.
Royal.ChargeHint: Once a month: urge a project on, and it finishes a week sooner. Use it from the project's card.
Royal.ChargeChat: {ruler} urges the work on: {project} will finish a week sooner.

Track.MissingNone: Every need for its size is met.
Track.PinnacleHint: One per kingdom. Needs a metropolis.
Track.StartBody: Build {stage}: {cost}. The {seat} runs it with {stat} skills.
Track.Heading: Tracks
Track.Summary: {built} of {total} built · {ready} you can build now

Trouble.None: Nothing is missing here, so there's no trouble to draw.
Trouble.Draw: Draw a trouble card here now (ignores the odds and the easy start)
Trouble.Possible: Trouble may strike at the start of each month until this is fixed.
Trouble.TenementsRisk: Tenements: crime is likelier here, and crime checks here take −1.
Trouble.Quiet: Easy start: no trouble cards for another {days} days.
Trouble.AllOut: Every trouble card this settlement can draw is already on a desk. Resolve one to draw it again.

Adjust.Title: Set the kingdom's numbers
Adjust.Hint: For results the module can't apply, house rulings or mistakes. Nothing else happens: no Fame is spent and no penalties are added on top.

Land.Heading: The land
Land.FoodLine: Farmland in {farms} hexes feeds {farms} a week; the settlements need {need}.
Land.NoCamps: No work sites yet (Treasurer: Establish a Work Site).
Land.Hint: Read from the Kingmaker map whenever it changes. Mark farms, roads, camps and settlements with the Kingmaker hex tools; the kingdom counts them here.
Land.NoMap: The Kingmaker module isn't active, so there's no map to read.
Land.FoodShort: The treasury buys the other {short} (−{bp} BP a week).
